reviews.body:
I checked which fields the scoping is accurate for: in `deeptutor/learning/teaching.py`, `evidence` is legitimately shared by both kinds (the preference path at the apply site keeps `text` and `evidence`, and `basis="learner_report"` requires it), so leaving it without an observation-only note is correct — the three fields you did annotate (`knowledge_point_id`, `strategy`, `outcome`) are the ones the preference path drops. The descriptions should also survive schema regeneration since they're plain Pydantic `Field(description=...)`, and the new test pins them against the generated tool definition rather than the model class, which is the right place to catch a future refactor silently dropping them.

One consideration for later: descriptions steer but don't enforce. If the model keeps sending `outcome`/`strategy` on preference updates anyway, they're silently ignored today (the apply path only reads `text`/`evidence` for preferences) — a follow-up could reject or warn on observation-only fields set for kind="preference", but that's a behavior change beyond this PR's scope.
